Every value carries its source, effective date and verification status from the 2026-10-06 research (v8-isone-complete/research/R1-R3 + REGISTER.md). status: verified | corrected (verified value that differs from the external review) | assumption (a cited default the user can change) | pending (rule not yet in force) | contingent (legal status unsettled) | unverifiable. The app shows the source on every figure that uses these.

interconnection._about: S3 (2026-10-06): every entry carries src, status and effective date from v8-isone-complete/research/R1-interconnection-isone.md (the REGISTER §1 rows). Read by rules/isone.js only; the app never types these numbers.

profile.note: eTariff version ID not verified (R1 Q-A); the compiled PDF retrieved 2026-10-06 is the text read.

small_generator_max_mw.note: Large Generating Facility = more than 20 MW; 20 MW or less follows Schedule 23.

alt.when: request already holds NRIS, or converts NR to CNR

readiness_deposit_initial.note: Only $300k of the $800k entry is cash; the $500k readiness deposit may be an LC or a bond.

deposit_in_lieu_site_control.applies: NRIS only, where a regulatory limitation applies
deposit_in_lieu_site_control.note: Cash, in addition to the entry deposits; refundable; 100% site control due within 180 days of the LGIA effective date.

readiness_floor.value: the total readiness deposit never falls below what is already posted: CRD_k = max(CRD paid, x_k × NU)
readiness_floor.note: No clause releases excess readiness deposit before withdrawal or LGIA; whether ISO-NE releases it in practice is open (R1 Q-E).

site_control_at_request.note: 100% at request. CNRIS has no exception; NRIS may post the deposit in lieu where a regulatory limitation applies.

request_window.next_window: cluster results meeting (or restudy results meeting) + 60 days, 30 days' public notice
request_window.note: Window dates per ISO Newswire 2026-09-18 and the ISO-NE Interconnection Process Guide; transition dates effective 2025-05-03 (ER25-2149).

report_meeting_business_days.note: Business days Mon–Fri; no holiday calendar is held.

facilities_study_days.waivable: elect within 20 days of the results meeting; only if no shared network upgrade or all sharers agree

facilities_study_agreement.note: Tendered within 5 business days of the 'no further restudy' notice; executed within 30 days.

lgia_tender_days.unit: days after FS comments or waiver notice

withdrawal_penalty.rule: max(study deposit, 2 × allocated study cost | 5% | 10% | 20% of network upgrades by phase), with exemptions
withdrawal_penalty.note: Pro forma adopted without modification ([F1] §IV.B.1.j). Paid from the readiness deposit; the unapplied deposit is refunded (§3.7).

withdrawal_penalty_exemptions.rule: no penalty if the network-upgrade cost in the most recent Cluster Restudy Report is more than 25% above the preceding report, or the Facilities Study Report more than 100% above the Cluster Study or Restudy Report; nor if the withdrawal does not materially affect any request in the same Cluster
withdrawal_penalty_exemptions.note: Strictly more than; the 25% test is measured on a Cluster Restudy Report only (no exemption off the first Cluster Study Report).

cost_allocation.share: impact ÷ Σ impact over participants with DFAX > 3%
cost_allocation.multi_element: a project's impact is the sum over elements of its highest impact on each

screening_thresholds.note: NCIS: record overloads at least 2% above the applicable rating; a project is associated if it raises flow by 2% and its DFAX is above 3%. CCIS: more than 10 MVA above rating, or at least 2%.

storage_charging_study_basis.value: net shoulder load (17,680 MW); storage charging is not studied at peak

ratings.note: Mapping of the DB's Rate A / Rate C columns to Normal / LTE is unverifiable from the DB; label as 'rating as stored'.

Using them for a charge cap is a GridSense assumption, not an ISO-NE storage rule.

thermal_screen._scope: GAPS §4.4 apparent-power screen. The pf bound is a sensitivity, never a study result.

fca_results.src: ISO-NE key stats, Results of the Annual FCAs; FCA 18 filing ER24-1290 (2024-02-21)

auction_after_fca18.value: Annual Capacity Auction (prompt, sealed-bid), first May 2028 for CCP 2028/29
auction_after_fca18.seasonal_mri: CAR-SA: ISO aims to file by end-2026 for CCP 2028/29

ccp_calendar.rule: CCP runs 1 Jun to 31 May. No forward auction after FCA 18: the prompt ACA is held in early May before each CCP; a resource must demonstrate commercial operation by the deadline (illustrative 5 April) or it misses that CCP's auction and can only sell through monthly qualification (MRA / bilateral). CCP 2030/31 is the first ACA after the CONE / Net CONE recalculation. No seven-year price lock for new entrants.
ccp_calendar.note: The 5 April demonstration deadline is the filing's illustrative calendar.

price_path_default.rule: flat bands from cited clears (FCA 18; ARA/MRA prices about $5, peak $8 in 2025); user-set; never escalated

qc_solar_default.basis: fleet current-rule QC 561 of 1,409 MW MCap; replace with a site profile

qc_storage_default.basis: fleet current-rule QC 3,862 of 3,877 MW MCap (PSH + batteries); a 2-h and a 4-h battery of equal MW get the same QC

qc_rule_intermittent.value: 5-summer average of median net output in HE14–HE18 plus CSC hours; FCA qualified capacity = summer QC

qc_seasons.rule: Summer Intermittent Reliability Hours Jun–Sep (HE14–HE18); winter Oct–May (HE18–HE19). FCA / ACA qualified capacity of an intermittent resource = summer QC; non-intermittent = lesser of summer and winter QC

mric_season_months.rule: CAR-SA prices summer and winter separately; the season split of the seasonal auction is not in R2, so the current QC rule's Jun–Sep / Oct–May months are used

rmri_preliminary.note: Preliminary values; a CAR-SA price is per kW of MRIC, never per kW of QC.

balancing_ratio_cap.note: FERC acceptance of the cap not confirmed.

csc_interval_min.src: MR1 §III.13.7.2.1 (a CSC exists in any 5-minute interval in which the RCPF sets the reserve price)

stop_loss.monthly_rule: PfP subtracted from the Capacity Base Payment in an Obligation Month is limited to FCA Starting Price × CSO (excludes PfP for output above CSO)
stop_loss.src: MR1 §III.13.7.3.1-2; ER26-3047 fn 7; FCA 18 filing ER24-1290 (starting price)
stop_loss.note: FCA 18 starting price. FCA 15–17 starting prices and the ACA Offer Price Cap (which replaces it from CCP 2028/29) are not held (R2 open questions R3, R6).

pfp.formula: PfP = (1/Y) Σ_events Σ_intervals PPR × (A_t − CSO × min(BR_e, 1)) / 12, with monthly and annual stop-loss

events._note: All seven Capacity Scarcity Conditions since 2018-06-01 (system 30-min reserve shortfall). Public interval source: ISO-NE Capacity Scarcity Condition Report CSV. start/end are 5-minute interval-beginning labels, so the window ends 5 minutes after the last label.

rows.note: Labels 17:45–19:20 span 20 intervals; the ISO slide table gives 110 minutes (22 intervals). The replay weights the 20 labelled intervals to 22.

events.src: ISO-NE OP-4 / CSC reports (URLs in R2 §B3)

da_as.closeout_rule: close-out per MWh of DA obligation = max(0, hourly Real-Time Hub price − strike); strike = max(forecast hourly RT Hub + $10, 0) or the daily distillate-CT floor if higher
da_as.note: Hourly RT Hub, not 5-minute node prices. DA A/S design under IMM review (memo 2026-02-04).

regulation_base_case.rule: Regulation is a saturated market (468 MW of ATRR for about 93 MW of requirement): 0 in the base case; the sensitivity bound is the pro-rata share MW ÷ (ATRR + MW) of the 2025 pool

intervals.rule: RT settles on 5-minute intervals at the node; DA hourly; deviations from DA schedules settle at RT prices; generators are credited the FER Price on DA energy obligations

da_premium_2025.rule: Mass Hub simple averages; the DA price includes the FER Price, so the LMP-only premium is about $2

hub_hedge.rule: Financial PPA settled at Mass Hub: R_PPA = Σ q × (K − LMP_hub); basis Σ g × (LMP_node − LMP_hub) stays with the seller
hub_hedge.src: R2 §D2; MR1 §III.2.7-2.8 (hub = average of the hub node set)

class1_acp.src: 225 CMR 14.08(4)(a)2 ($40 from CY2023, no CPI index); R2 §E1

class1_scope.rule: Class I RECs come from RPS Class I generation only; stand-alone storage earns none. GridSense models the Massachusetts market only (the $40 ACP also applies in CT and RI, not modelled)

rows.name: Firm Contract Demand Service
rows.text: Permanent, firm, fixed contract MW that cannot be exceeded; same curtailment priority as RNS/LNS load; every identified network upgrade must be in service first

rows.name: Non-Firm Contract Demand Service
rows.text: Permanent non-firm service, studied with the load's flexibility to minimise upgrades; billed on actual demand at the monthly peak; curtailable

rows.name: Interim Contract Demand Service
rows.text: Temporary non-firm service before the upgrades are done, billed as NFCDS; converts to FCDS when its requirements (upgrades included) are met

services.note: A large load cannot take traditional RNS/LNS, and one point of delivery cannot be split across services.
services.src: ISO-NE RC/TC deck 2026-08-18/19 slides 10-31; PTO-AC deck 2026-09-15 slides 7, 14 (R3 D5)

study_days.note: Large-load study from a complete application; rolling applications, outside the generator cluster studies. Facilities study and construction durations are not published.

cra.formula: max(0, carrying charge × Large Load Network Upgrades (excluding Similar Upgrades) − FCDS charge)
cra.carrying_charge_note: Not published. The PTO-AC deck's worked example uses an illustrative carrying charge; it is not a PTO rate and is never used.
cra.similar_upgrades: Upgrades duplicating RSP-list projects are excluded from the CRA; the RSP-list match is not held, so the study cost may include them.
cra.llif: Sole-use Large Load Interconnection Facilities are recovered separately (not in the CRA).
cra.src: PTO-AC 'Proposed Large Load Cost Recovery Agreement' 2026-09-15 slides 7-13, 16-17 (R3 D7, R3 §3.4)

rows.text: Bring your own new generation (BYONG): designated resources before FCDS; the large load is excluded from the Installed Capacity Requirement. Cost = self-supply cost; detailed rules in 2027.
Interim service may start before BYONG is met; the self-supply cost follows at conversion to FCDS.
No BYONG requirement (curtailable). FCM treatment of large loads while BYONG detail is pending is an open question.
